name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: Peters holds a $2.6 million-to-$4,000 cash advantage over Cohen
District leans Democratic by about ten points and Peters is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Peters near 96 percent to win
No public general-election polling exists for the race
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a D+10 district, an incumbent with $2.6 million on hand facing a challenger who has raised about $4,000, and market pricing near 96 percent for Peters. With no contrary polling or ratings, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late outside spending, challenger advertising, or polling showing Cohen within single digits would be the first sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a San Diego-area district that has leaned about ten points Democratic in recent partisan races. He has raised more than $2.1 million and holds $2.6 million on hand, while Republican Steve Cohen has reported roughly $4,000 in total receipts and drawn no outside support. Peters advanced through the top-two primary, and prediction markets price his chances near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and market pricing. Those signals all align, pointing to an expected margin of roughly twenty points. Uncertainty is somewhat elevated without polling, but a margin of this size leaves only a small chance of an upset. A surge of outside money for Cohen or an unusually low-turnout electorate would be needed to make the race competitive.
